requirements.requirement: Nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1, stored as dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1
requirements.summary: A backup script (/usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup.sh) streams a tar.gz of node2's /srv/inventory/data over SSH into a dated archive in /var/backups/inventory on node1, scheduled via /etc/cron.d/inventory-backup at 02:00 daily. A manual run produced inventory-data-2026-08-26.tar.gz whose extracted contents (items.csv, last-updated.txt) exactly matched the live source data on node2. A second end-to-end run after both node restarts also succeeded and matched source content.

requirements.requirement: Retain the last 7 days of archives
requirements.summary: The script prunes with `ls -1t ... | awk 'NR>keep' | xargs rm -f` where keep=7. Executor seeded 9 dated archives (8 synthetic + 1 real) and re-ran the script; exactly the 7 most recent were retained and the 2 oldest were pruned, directly proving the retention logic. Synthetic archives were subsequently cleaned up, leaving only the real backup.

requirements.requirement: Backup runs automatically every night (scheduled execution mechanism in place and active)
requirements.summary: /etc/cron.d/inventory-backup schedules the script at 02:00 daily as user antrieb, logging to /var/log/inventory-backup.log. crond was enabled and confirmed active both before and after node1's restart, showing the schedule is persistent and the service is running (though no evidence of an actual 02:00 unattended firing was captured, which is expected given the compressed test window).

overall_summary: The executor implemented a working nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to /var/backups/inventory on node1 with correct dated-archive naming, verified content fidelity, and directly demonstrated the 7-day retention policy by seeding and pruning test archives. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed for both nodes with clear before/after boot-identity changes, cron/crond persistence, and functional post-restart backups, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary residue or damaged state was found.
limitations: No evidence of an actual unattended 02:00 cron firing was captured (only manual invocations of the script were observed), since the test window did not span a real overnight cycle.

Package-health checks timed out on both nodes in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so native package consistency could not be verified; this predates the executor's actions and is not attributable to it.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task setup, functional verification, or the mandated restart protocol. Synthetic retention-test archives (cmd-678fe26f65954ab3) were a bounded, low-risk mutation used to directly prove the 7-day pruning behavior and were fully removed afterward (cmd-22027d80d9754db2), leaving no residue. Creation of representative source data on node2 (cmd-b99ec09fcbc04cd7) was a necessary prerequisite since /srv/inventory/data did not exist. SSH key setup and /etc/hosts entries (cmd-64bb6be713504930, cmd-d73f06a4959342d0) were required for the node2-to-node1 backup transport. One SSH connectivity attempt failed due to an unsupported StrictHostKeyChecking option (cmd-95c28542027e4f51) and was immediately corrected (cmd-45cf2ab7d1504cd2) with no lasting effect. Lifecycle diffs show only expected post-reboot artifacts (new boot_id, reboot.log, refreshed systemd-private tmp dirs, ephemeral PID changes in socket listings) with no failed services or unexplained residue on either node.
